level1_topics.topic_definition: Conduct of relations with other nations: treaties, diplomacy, neutrality, alliances, hemispheric and great-power policy, foreign aid, and international organizations.
The waging of wars and military campaigns, reports on operations, and the raising, equipping, and honoring of the armed forces and veterans.
Monetary policy, coinage and the mint, specie, paper currency, the gold standard, national and state banks, and financial crises.
Regulation of foreign and interstate commerce, tariffs, reciprocity, navigation laws, and control of corporate monopoly.
Government revenue, the public debt, appropriations, taxes, budgets, deficits, and federal spending.
The general economic condition, employment, wages and labor relations, poverty and welfare, health and old-age security, and prosperity of ordinary Americans.
Farming and farm prices, disposal and settlement of public lands, and conservation of natural resources and the environment.
Federal support for roads, canals, harbors, energy, and other public works and large-scale national development projects.
Slavery and emancipation, racial equality and voting rights, discrimination, and the admission and treatment of immigrants.
Relations with Indian tribes: treaties, hostilities, removal, reservations, allotment, and efforts at assimilation.
Enforcement of federal law, suppression of insurrection, crime and courts, and morals legislation in the Territories.
The constitutional structure of the government: federalism and union, executive power, civil-service reform, territorial organization and statehood, and the integrity of elections.
Non-policy ceremonial speech: eulogies, tributes to founders and heroes, anniversary commemorations, and national mourning.
Non-policy personal speech: the president's humility about office, autobiographical storytelling, humor, and boasting of achievements.
Non-policy housekeeping: routine departmental reports, postal operations, and the mechanics of executive-legislative business.
Non-policy appeals to Providence, faith, patriotism, civic ideals, and the shared moral character of the nation.
Non-policy political combat: attacks on opponents and parties, campaign debate, press-conference exchanges, and clashes with the media.

actual_speaker_invocation_paragraph_coun.definition: Distinct keyed paragraphs in which the accepted invocation evidence records the actual speaker naming the former-president target.
actual_speaker_invocation_paragraph_coun.interpretation: Descriptive corpus evidence only; not a normalized rate, historical completeness claim, influence measure, confidence score, or causal claim.
actual_speaker_invocation_paragraph_coun.population: Resolved, analysis-eligible, former-president, non-self rows in the accepted actual-speaker invocation overlay.

actual_speaker_topic_contribution.definition: Topic-bearing eligible paragraphs attributed to the president divided by all eligible paragraphs carrying that topic across presidents in the scope.
actual_speaker_topic_contribution.unit: Distinct paragraph presence; appearances are distinct (doc_name, actual-speaker profile ID) receipts.

actual_speaker_topic_presence.definition: Topic-bearing eligible paragraphs attributed to the president divided by all eligible paragraphs attributed to that president in the scope.
actual_speaker_topic_presence.unit: Distinct paragraph presence; appearances are distinct (doc_name, actual-speaker profile ID) receipts.

topic_scope_share.definition: All eligible paragraphs carrying the topic divided by all eligible actual-president paragraphs in the scope.
topic_scope_share.unit: Distinct paragraph presence; appearances are distinct (doc_name, actual-speaker profile ID) receipts.

policies.invocation_population_policy: Resolved, analysis-eligible, former-president, non-self accepted invocation rows attributed through the speaker overlay.
policies.invocation_target_status_limitation: target_status is determined from corpus speech dates rather than an independent legal-term calendar.

legacy_issue_methods.legacy_distinctive_vocabulary_v3: Current legacy method: attach a term after at least two issue uses when its per-word issue rate is at least 1.5× its rate in the president's text.
legacy_issue_methods.legacy_stance_v3: Current legacy method: count fixed era-portable phrases in issue paragraphs; require eight matches and use a 60/40 split for a directional label.

legacy_issue_thresholds.era_peer_fallback: All other presidents when fewer than two window peers exist.

policies.multi_label_counting_policy: Count each distinct normalized Level 2 topic once per paragraph and each distinct derived Level 1 parent once per paragraph. Preserve one full paragraph-presence membership for every topic; do not divide a paragraph fractionally. Topic shares are non-additive and may sum above 100%.

population_labels.connections: Eligible paragraphs attributed to the actual speaker.
population_labels.core_profile: Source documents assigned to the president.

policies.topic_evidence_selection_policy: Deterministic audit examples, not representative samples or historical proof: select the first, lower-middle, and last qualifying actual-speaker appearance chronologically, deduplicate appearances, and take the lowest qualifying paragraph index within each selected appearance.
policies.topic_free_denominator_policy: All eligible actual-president paragraphs, including topic-free paragraphs, remain in president and scope denominators; topic-free paragraphs create no membership and no edge.
policies.topic_interpretation_policy: Descriptive AI-assigned topic presence in speaker-audited Miller Center paragraphs. It is not historical validation, model confidence, presidential intent, importance, influence, causality, policy success, or representation of the public or presidency as a whole.
policies.topic_selection_policy: Python precomputes focal topics and peers in the declared measure/order; peer selection is round-robin and never browser-derived.
